objective: Integrate BUKLOD MAIN production-compatible AdMob native first-view timeout recovery and exact Cluster Admin Check In Today review into the existing non-Season 2 production-intake source, without deploying unsafe or unverified changes.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: Live production Supabase 2026-11-22 ~09:26-09:29 Asia/Manila, app 1.3.6 build30 runtime1.3.2 ADMob Native had 260 requests, 51 loads and 112 native load timeouts during rolling 60m; banner 95 requests/60 loads; new cluster-review functions not installed and Mission Worker one check-in pending. Main ecd34228dd24f07a47ba397bb1c29199aac51779 is code baseline only; independently recorded prior EAS production source 98fda684f8a322ba0095adda06899534fdcfa6fe is not freshly fingerprint-verified. Owner explicitly requested a consolidated production release; this is DEV/RC preparation, not release proof.
chosenApproach: Use one bounded session-local shared NativeAd failure circuit after three distinct placement failures in 60s (2m banner preference, immediate recovery on actual native SDK success). Keep per-placement 2-failure/5m logic, native prewarm cap, consent, cooldown, impression event provenance. Carry exact-Cluster attendance authorization and UI from previously verified PR #1086 into nonseason2 production intake PR #1082; DO NOT apply SQL or publish until isolated DB and real Android/OTA gates.
selectionRationale: Cross-dashboard native timeouts indicate common SDK/network/inventory degradation; shared bounded fallback lowers repeated first-view delay without extra ad requests. Backend Cluster Admin role is enforced on exact scope server-side, not client-only or System Admin.
alternativeApproaches: Disable AdMob production units or ads_all kill switch: rejected because it immediately eliminates legitimate inventory and revenue.
Retry all native placements aggressively or parallel-load both banner and native: rejected due duplicate demand, policy/fill and navigation-regression risk.
Publish Genesis/Godot 2.0.x directly to production 1.3.2 runtime: rejected because incompatible native module/ABI and active Season 2 release safety requirements.
